No, this statement is incorrect.

Women in Switzerland gained the right to vote and stand for election at the federal level in **1971**, following a referendum held on February 7, 1971, in which Swiss men approved the change by a narrow majority.

However, it is also incorrect to say that "all cantons had already voted uniformly in favor of it in 1971." In fact, the cantonal votes varied significantly in 1971:

*   Some cantons approved women's suffrage immediately in 1971.
*   Others approved it in subsequent years (e.g., Geneva in 1960, Basel-City in 1966).
*   The last canton, Appenzell Innerrhoden, did not grant women the right to vote at the cantonal level until **1991**, following a federal court ruling that forced it to do so.

Thus, while the federal right to vote was established in 1971, cantonal implementation was not uniform and was completed much later in some areas.
